tagline: Grid.js is a small, elegant, framework-agnostic table library focused on the essentials, MIT-licensed.
oneLineVerdict: Grid.js is a lovely lightweight pick for search / sort / paginate. SvGrid is the fuller, Svelte-native grid when you need virtualization, editing, grouping, or large datasets.
alternativeIntro: Grid.js is deliberately small and covers the essentials well. People outgrow it at the same points every time: virtualization for large datasets, inline editing, row grouping and server-side data. SvGrid has those, and keeps a headless core so a simple table does not have to carry the weight of the full component.
intro: Grid.js keeps a deliberately small surface: search, sort, pagination, and basic server-side data, rendered through a tiny vanilla-JS core with framework wrappers. It is MIT-licensed and easy to learn.
SvGrid trades that minimalism for depth: a Svelte-5-native render component with virtualization, an Excel-style filter menu, inline editing, grouping, tree data, and an imperative API.
similarities: Search, sort, and pagination out of the box.
svgridAdvantages: Svelte 5 native instead of a vanilla core + wrapper.
Row + column virtualization for large datasets.
Excel-style filters, inline editing, grouping, tree, master/detail.
competitorAdvantages: Tiny footprint if all you need is search / sort / paginate.
Very fast to learn for a simple table.

competitor.note: vanilla JavaScript with React, Angular and Vue wrappers

whenToChooseSvGrid: You need virtualization, editing, grouping, or tree data.
You are on Svelte 5 and want a native component.
You expect the table to grow beyond search / sort / paginate.
whenToChooseCompetitor: You only need search / sort / paginate over a modest dataset.
You want the smallest possible footprint.

youLose: A very small library for a simple table on any page.
Wrappers for React, Angular and Vue.

pricing.summary: Grid.js is MIT, free and open source; no licence is sold

bottomLine: Grid.js is a lovely minimalist table for search, sort, and paginate. When you outgrow that - virtualization, editing, grouping, tree - SvGrid is the Svelte-native grid that already covers it.

faq.question: SvGrid vs Grid.js - which should I choose?
faq.answer: Grid.js for a small table that only needs search, sort, and paginate; SvGrid when you need virtualization, editing, Excel-style filters, or grouping.

faq.question: Is SvGrid heavier than Grid.js?
faq.answer: Yes, because it does much more. For a trivial table Grid.js is lighter; for a real data grid SvGrid pays for itself.

faq.question: Does SvGrid support server-side data like Grid.js?
faq.answer: Yes - externalSort and externalFilter, plus the onSortingChange and onFiltersChange events.

sources.evidences: Free and open source under MIT; works with React, Angular, Vue and vanilla JavaScript; an extensible data pipeline
